=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Two points before the substance

**1. "FINAL, not to be re-opened" does not bind us.** The Seller's preamble says these positions were settled at principal level and are FINAL. That is the Seller's assertion in its own draft. I have no record of such agreement. Several positions also conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. For example, Bluefen is called "addressed" but para 2 says no consent exists, and Riverlark is to be released "following Completion" in a debt-free deal. **Please confirm with Wattlebridge's principals whether anything was actually agreed.** Until then, treat every point as open.

**2. The "market standard" framing is self-serving.** A 10–20% cap and roughly 1% basket can be reasonable for *general* warranties. The draft goes much further. It applies those limits to title, capacity, tax, known issues and "all Claims of any nature". It also combines them with general data-room disclosure and a buyer-knowledge bar. Taken together, the package would leave Wattlebridge almost no recourse for the issues we already know about.

---

## A. Structural issues (highest priority)

These interact with each other. Together they would neutralise almost every protection.

### A1. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3): reject
- It bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew. It also bars anything merely **"discoverable"** from the data room or public records, which is constructive knowledge.
- Every known issue (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) is in the data room. This clause would therefore extinguish claims on exactly the matters that most need protection.
- **Push for:** the reverse position. The Buyer's knowledge, actual or constructive, and any investigation do not reduce or prevent a claim, except to the extent of matters **Fairly Disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter.

### A2. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Sch 7): reject
- It discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- This fixes the Seller's warranty risk at the Buyer's due-diligence cost, and it pairs with A1 to the same effect.
- **Push for:**
  - Only specific disclosures in the letter count.
  - They must be **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its impact**.
  - Data-room documents count only where a specific disclosure expressly cross-refers to them.
  - Delete the public records disclosure.
  - Fundamental warranties and the tax warranties cannot be disclosed against.
  - Para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it does not dilute the fair-disclosure standard.

### A3. "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13) and limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5): reject as drafted
- As drafted, the cap, basket, de minimis and 18-month period would apply to:
  - title and capacity claims;
  - tax;
  - specific indemnities;
  - leakage and price adjustment;
  - breach of completion obligations and covenants;
  - arguably fraud.
- **Push for express carve-outs from all limitations for:**
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment (by the Seller, its officers, or Company management before Completion);
  - Fundamental Warranties;
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity, which get their own regime;
  - specific indemnities;
  - breach of pre-Completion and Completion covenants;
  - leakage and price adjustment;
  - the Seller's payment obligations.
- **Non-reliance:** liability for fraud cannot be excluded under NSW law. Non-reliance clauses also do not reliably defeat claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. We should still not concede the point. Delete "of any nature" and include the fraud and misleading-conduct carve-out expressly.

### A4. Fundamental warranties under the general cap and time limit: reject
- Under the draft, if the Seller does not own the shares, the Buyer pays AUD 24m and can recover only AUD 4.8m, and only for 18 months. That is untenable.
- **Push for:**
  - Title, capacity, authority, solvency and capital-structure warranties capped at **100% of price**.
  - Claim period of **7 years** (or the statutory limitation period).
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - Not disclosable against.

### A5. Tax "settled under the general regime": reject
- **Push for:**
  - A standalone **tax indemnity/covenant** for pre-Completion tax periods.
  - Cap of 100% of price.
  - No threshold.
  - Claim period of at least the relevant ATO and State Revenue amendment period plus a buffer. Seven years is a common ask.
  - Conduct-of-claims provisions.
- Bonus on-costs (C3) fall squarely within this.

---

## B. Financial limits (cl 12.1–12.3)

| Term | Seller | Buyer position | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Seek 30–50%, or accept 20% **only** if A1–A5 are fixed and specific indemnities sit outside the cap | 20% is defensible only for general warranties with proper carve-outs |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 10,000; **related claims aggregate** | Prevents splitting one issue into small claims (relevant to Sandbar, C5) |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | **Tipping** basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded) at around AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%) | An "excess only" basket on top of a 20% cap keeps the first AUD 250k of loss permanently with the Buyer |
| General time limit | 18 months | 18–24 months is acceptable; at least one full audit cycle post-Completion | Reasonable for general warranties only |

**Security for claims:** Harbourglass Ventures is a fund-style vehicle that may distribute sale proceeds. Seek one of:
- a **retention or escrow** (e.g. 10% for the warranty period plus amounts tied to specific indemnities);
- a parent or fund guarantee;
- W&I insurance. Note that W&I typically excludes *known* matters, so the specific indemnities below remain necessary regardless.

---

## C. Specific transaction issues

### C1. Bluefen (approx. 30% of FY26 revenue, AUD 3.6m): critical
- The Seller says the consent is "addressed". Its own Disclosure Letter (para 2) says **no final written consent exists and the clause 11.3 conditions are not evidenced as satisfied**.
- The proposed mechanics are weak. "Reasonable endeavours" plus "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" could be met by a conditional or qualified consent, or one that does not satisfy clause 11.3.
- **Push for:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's **unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably)**.
  - Evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - No adverse variation to contract terms.
  - The condition is **waivable only by the Buyer**.
  - The Seller uses best/all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer participation in approaches to Bluefen.
  - A sunset date and Buyer termination right.
  - If the Buyer waives the condition: a specific indemnity or price-adjustment mechanism for loss of the contract within a defined period, outside the limitations.

### C2. Riverlark facility (approx. AUD 3.2m): critical
- A release "following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- Para 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge. The change-of-control clause (8.1) may be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push for:**
  - The facility treated as **Debt** and repaid **from the Completion funds flow** under a payout letter.
  - Completion deliverables:
    - signed deed of release;
    - PPSR financing change statements or discharges;
    - release of any guarantees, and of any share security over the shares (check whether Riverlark holds security over the shares; see C9).
  - A waiver of clause 8.1 pending repayment.
  - An indemnity for any amount outstanding.

### C3. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000): high
- The Seller calls these "a matter for the Seller", yet they are **excluded from the funds flow**. If they are Company obligations, the Buyer funds them post-Completion.
- They are also likely to attract on-costs not yet quantified:
  - PAYG withholding;
  - superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025, subject to the bonus terms and ordinary-time-earnings analysis);
  - NSW payroll tax;
  - workers' compensation.
- **Push for:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt** and deducted from price, or paid through payroll at Completion from Seller funds.
  - Where continued-employment conditions defer payment, an equivalent amount retained in escrow.
  - A specific indemnity.

### C4. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004, DD-010): high
- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials passes only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. No payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.
- The Company may therefore **not own IP it uses**.
- The proposed indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment". It ignores:
  - the ownership gap;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - remediation and re-development costs;
  - any other unpaid SOW3 fees.
- **Push for:**
  - All SOW3 fees paid before Completion, or retained from price.
  - Evidence of cleared payment.
  - A **signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay** as a Completion deliverable or CP.
  - An IP warranty that is not limited to the general regime.
  - A broad specific indemnity for all loss from any failure of the Company to own SOW3 materials, outside the limitations.

### C5. DD-006 export/privacy incident (approx. 1,240 records): high
- The Seller's statement that it is "not expected to be material" is unsupported. Para 6 itself says access, scope and notification obligations are **unknown** and the investigation is **preliminary**.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment, generally within 30 days. The disclosure is dated 22 September 2026 and it is now early November. **We should ask when the incident was discovered and whether an assessment has been completed.** If not, there may be a compliance failure on top of the incident.
- Recent Privacy Act reforms (including the statutory privacy tort and expanded OAIC enforcement powers) increase the potential exposure.
- **Push for:**
  - Full investigation materials and any forensic report.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and consult the Buyer.
  - A specific warranty on the facts and actions taken.
  - A **specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims, outside the limitations and the knowledge bar.

### C6. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; AUD 330,000): medium
- These are three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, and the Disclosure Letter says to read them **together**. Each sits below the AUD 250k basket individually.
- That raises two questions:
  - whether the split is designed to stay under thresholds, whether claim thresholds or internal and SPA conduct-of-business approval limits;
  - whether the commitments are avoidable.
- The Seller's "ordinary course" label is contradicted by para 8, which does not say this.
- **Push for:**
  - Copies and dates of each renewal.
  - Confirmation of whether they were entered after the Accounts Date or locked-box date (if applicable).
  - Termination rights and any prepayments.
  - Aggregation of related claims.
  - A conduct-of-business restriction treating related commitments as one.
  - If they were not in the ordinary course or not approved: treat them as Debt or leakage, or obtain an indemnity.

### C7. Office lease (DD-007): low/medium
- Only a notification obligation is identified.
- **Action:** confirm against the lease text that no consent is triggered by change of control. Make notice (and any required landlord acknowledgment) a Completion deliverable.

### C8. Mossvale (DD-009): low/medium
- Only an assignment restriction is identified.
- **Action:** review whether the contract deems a change of control to be an assignment. If it does, add Mossvale consent as a CP or deliverable. Either way, obtain a warranty that no material contract has a change-of-control trigger other than those disclosed.

### C9. Title (DD-012): high (verification)
- A share register maintained by the Company is not sufficient on its own. Para 10 confirms the Seller has not verified it for the Buyer's benefit.
- **Actions:**
  - ASIC company extract.
  - Constitution and any shareholders' agreement.
  - Confirm no options, convertible notes, SAFEs, ESOP awards or pre-emptive rights. This matters given the employee bonus arrangements.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company. Check whether Riverlark holds security over the shares.
- **Completion deliverables:** share transfer forms, share certificates, board resolutions, waivers of pre-emption, and releases of any security.
- **Warranty:** uncapped (100% of price) and 7 years, per A4.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. Buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3). Replace with a pro-buyer knowledge clause.
2. General disclosure of the data room and public records. Allow specific, fair disclosure only.
3. Fundamental warranties under the general cap and time limit. Use 100% of price and 7 years instead.
4. "Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature". Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and leakage.
5. Tax under the general regime. Use a standalone tax indemnity.

**Restructure:**

6. **Bluefen:** Buyer-only waivable CP for unconditional consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3. Seller uses best endeavours. Sunset and termination right.
7. **Riverlark:** repay at Completion from funds flow as Debt. Deed of release and PPSR discharges as Completion deliverables.
8. **Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs):** add to the funds flow as a price deduction, with escrow and an indemnity.
9. **Ironquay:** pay all SOW3 fees and obtain a confirmatory assignment before Completion. Broad IP indemnity.
10. **DD-006:** full disclosure of investigation materials, pre-Completion NDB compliance covenant, specific privacy indemnity.
11. **Sandbar:** full documents and dates, aggregation of related claims, debt/leakage treatment if out of the ordinary course.

**Negotiable within range:**

12. General cap: 20% is acceptable only if items 1–5 are fixed and specific indemnities sit outside it. Otherwise seek 30–50%.
13. Basket: change to tipping, at around 0.5–1%. De minimis around AUD 10k, with aggregation of related claims.
14. 18–24 months for general warranties.
15. Retention/escrow or guarantee from Harbourglass. Consider W&I, noting it will not cover known issues.

**Confirm or verify:**

16. With principals: was anything actually agreed?
17. DD-006 discovery date and NDB assessment status.
18. Lease and Mossvale change-of-control wording.
19. Title searches (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, equity instruments).

**Assumptions and limits:** I have reviewed only the Seller's summary positions and the Disclosure Letter, not the underlying SPA text or data-room documents (DD-002 to DD-012). Clause references are as the Seller described them. The statutory points (Privacy Act, ACL, superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax) are stated at a general level and should be confirmed by the relevant specialists before being relied on in the mark-up.

If helpful, I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or draft the carve-out, knowledge and specific indemnity clauses next.

  - Bonuses plus all on-costs treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt** and deducted from price, or paid through payroll at Completion from Seller funds.
  - Where continued-employment conditions defer payment, an equivalent amount retained in escrow.
  - A specific indemnity.

### C4. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004, DD-010): high
- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials passes only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. No payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.
- The Company may therefore **not own IP it uses**.
- The proposed indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment". It ignores:
  - the ownership gap;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - remediation and re-development costs;
  - any other unpaid SOW3 fees.
- **Push for:**
  - All SOW3 fees paid before Completion, or retained from price.
  - Evidence of cleared payment.
  - A **signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay** as a Completion deliverable or CP.
  - An IP warranty that is not limited to the general regime.
  - A broad specific indemnity for all loss from any failure of the Company to own SOW3 materials, outside the limitations.

### C5. DD-006 export/privacy incident (approx. 1,240 records): high
- The Seller's statement that it is "not expected to be material" is unsupported. Para 6 itself says access, scope and notification obligations are **unknown** and the investigation is **preliminary**.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment, generally within 30 days. The disclosure is dated 22 September 2026 and it is now early November. **We should ask when the incident was discovered and whether an assessment has been completed.** If not, there may be a compliance failure on top of the incident.
- Recent Privacy Act reforms (including the statutory privacy tort and expanded OAIC enforcement powers) increase the potential exposure.
- **Push for:**
  - Full investigation materials and any forensic report.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and consult the Buyer.
  - A specific warranty on the facts and actions taken.
  - A **specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims, outside the limitations and the knowledge bar.

### C6. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; AUD 330,000): medium
- These are three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, and the Disclosure Letter says to read them **together**. Each sits below the AUD 250k basket individually.
- That raises two questions:
  - whether the split is designed to stay under thresholds, whether claim thresholds or internal and SPA conduct-of-business approval limits;
  - whether the commitments are avoidable.
- The Seller's "ordinary course" label is contradicted by para 8, which does not say this.
- **Push for:**
  - Copies and dates of each renewal.
  - Confirmation of whether they were entered after the Accounts Date or locked-box date (if applicable).
  - Termination rights and any prepayments.
  - Aggregation of related claims.
  - A conduct-of-business restriction treating related commitments as one.
  - If they were not in the ordinary course or not approved: treat them as Debt or leakage, or obtain an indemnity.

### C7. Office lease (DD-007): low/medium
- Only a notification obligation is identified.
- **Action:** confirm against the lease text that no consent is triggered by change of control. Make notice (and any required landlord acknowledgment) a Completion deliverable.

### C8. Mossvale (DD-009): low/medium
- Only an assignment restriction is identified.

### C9. Title (DD-012): high (verification)
- A share register maintained by the Company is not sufficient on its own. Para 10 confirms the Seller has not verified it for the Buyer's benefit.
- **Actions:**

  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company. Check whether Riverlark holds security over the shares.
- **Completion deliverables:** share transfer forms, share certificates, board resolutions, waivers of pre-emption, and releases of any security.
- **Warranty:** uncapped (100% of price) and 7 years, per A4.

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. Buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3). Replace with a pro-buyer knowledge clause.
2. General disclosure of the data room and public records. Allow specific, fair disclosure only.
3. Fundamental warranties under the general cap and time limit. Use 100% of price and 7 years instead.
4. "Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature". Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and leakage.
5. Tax under the general regime. Use a standalone tax indemnity.

**Restructure:**

6. **Bluefen:** Buyer-only waivable CP for unconditional consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3. Seller uses best endeavours. Sunset and termination right.
7. **Riverlark:** repay at Completion from funds flow as Debt. Deed of release and PPSR discharges as Completion deliverables.
8. **Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs):** add to the funds flow as a price deduction, with escrow and an indemnity.
9. **Ironquay:** pay all SOW3 fees and obtain a confirmatory assignment before Completion. Broad IP indemnity.
10. **DD-006:** full disclosure of investigation materials, pre-Completion NDB compliance covenant, specific privacy indemnity.
11. **Sandbar:** full documents and dates, aggregation of related claims, debt/leakage treatment if out of the ordinary course.

**Negotiable within range:**

12. General cap: 20% is acceptable only if items 1–5 are fixed and specific indemnities sit outside it. Otherwise seek 30–50%.
13. Basket: change to tipping, at around 0.5–1%. De minimis around AUD 10k, with aggregation of related claims.
14. 18–24 months for general warranties.
15. Retention/escrow or guarantee from Harbourglass. Consider W&I, noting it will not cover known issues.

**Confirm or verify:**

16. With principals: was anything actually agreed?
17. DD-006 discovery date and NDB assessment status.
18. Lease and Mossvale change-of-control wording.
19. Title searches (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, equity instruments).
